newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals mixed as imports clog port.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals mixed as imports clog port.

text.p: Indian metals prices on Wednesday were mixed as imports clogged the Bombay port with truckers strike on its ninth day without an end in sight, dealers said.
"About 1,000/1,200 tonnes of the imported metals are piled up at the Bombay port," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
He said dealers were facing shortage of ready stock as there was no transportation due to the strike.
Dealers said aluminium prices gained while other base metals were steady in a narrow trading range.
"Trading volumes overall remained low on account of the absence of fresh arrivals of metals (imported and domestic) in the market due to the strike," a dealer said.

Aluminium gained by 25 rupees at 7,475 rupees per quintal on reports of a price hike by Indian producers. Producers are said to have raised selling prices of aluminium by 4,000/5,000 rupees per tonne.

Copper was remained steady at 13,500 rupees, zinc at 7,850 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal. Tin was available at the previous level of 31,600 rupees and nickel at 36,800 rupees per quintal but trading was low.
